The European Court of Human Rights (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001) held by 9 votes to 8 that there was no violation of Article 6(1), because the UK courts' application of the State Immunity Act 1978 to bar Mr Al-Adsani's torture damages claim against Kuwait pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate, and it also found no violation of Article 3 or Article 13. The shared note is wrong: the Court did not treat sovereign immunity as automatically overriding Convention guarantees, but weighed proportionality, and the dissenting judges would have found a violation of Article 6.

CONFIDENCE: 85
